facts.statement: Phasmagyps is an extinct genus of New World vulture from the family Cathartidae known from a single Oligocene fossil found in Colorado.
facts.quote: Phasmagyps, is an extinct genus of New World vulture in the family Cathartidae, known from one Oligocene fossil found in Colorado.

facts.statement: The genus contains one described species, Phasmagyps patritus, which is possibly the oldest known New World vulture.
facts.quote: The genus contains a single described species, Phasmagyps patritus which is possibly the oldest New World vulture known

facts.statement: The placement of Phasmagyps within the family Cathartidae has been questioned by researchers.
facts.quote: though its placement in the family Cathartidae has been questioned

facts.statement: The type specimen of Phasmagyps is a single fragmentary fossil bone housed in the Colorado Museum of Natural History with catalog number 1078.
facts.quote: Phasmagyps is known from a single fragmentary fossil bone, the holotype housed in the paleontology collections of the Colorado Museum of Natural History in Boulder, Colorado and given the number 1078.

facts.statement: The fossil was collected in 1923 by Philip Reinheinter from the Weld County Trigonias quarry.
facts.quote: In 1923 Philip Reinheinter collected the specimen from the Weld County Trigonias quarry

facts.statement: In 2005, Marcelo Stucchi and Steven Emslie maintained the placement of Phasmagyps in Cathartidae and noted it as the oldest member of the family in the Americas.
facts.quote: In their 2005 description of a Peruvian fossil, Marcelo Stucchi and Steven Emslie noted the disputed nature of Phasmagyps, but maintained the placement in Cathartidae and noted the genus as the oldest member of the family in the Americas.

facts.statement: When first described, Phasmagyps was estimated to be one-third larger than the modern Black vulture.
facts.quote: When first described by Wetmore, Phasmagyps was described as being one third larger than the modern Black vulture, Coragyps atratus.

facts.statement: James Ducey's 1992 paper contradicts the original size estimate, stating Phasmagyps was not much larger than the Black Vulture.
facts.quote: This is contradicted by James Ducey's 1992 paper which lists Phasmagyps as being "not much larger than the Black Vulture".

facts.statement: The preserved fossil has a largest diameter of 17.9 mm around the outer condyle and a width of 14.9 mm across the condyles.
facts.quote: As preserved, the largest diameter of the bone is 17.9 mm around the outer condyle, and the width across the condyles is 14.9 mm.

facts.statement: Phasmagyps lived during the Priabonian stage, approximately 37 to 33.9 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Priabonian to Priabonian (37 to 33.9 million years ago)

facts.statement: Phasmagyps is classified within the subfamily Vulturinae.
Phasmagyps belongs to the family Cathartidae.
